scope: One matched diagnostic repeat per case/model: Restaurants 8 on Luna, then Kiva 4 on Terra. 24 questions; different cases across models. No statistical significance or general accuracy claim.
conclusion: No accuracy or state-error improvement demonstrated. No historical-state actions were used. Luna failure starts in Task 3 artifact selection and formulas, then cascades. Terra updates/counterfactuals are numerically correct; initial-answer reporting and judge interpretation remain concerns.

validation.original_callback_errors: KeyErrors returned in 1.8846 and 1.7251 seconds; intentionally unfixed submitted formulas
validation.deletion_safety: Slow writer close remains pending; failed writes drain and close, then fail the completion future.
validation.limitation: The shutdown tests verify ordering, slow closure and surfaced failures. The close wait still has no independent service deadline; a storage flush that never returns can delay HTTP completion. No such delay occurred here.

main_failure_patterns: Task 3 created an incorrect operating-decision state by building the top-commission expansion with an unsorted limit and by applying the diagnose rule with the commercial gate in the wrong place; later tasks reused that state.
The first customer view confused high-value-customer count share with high-value-customer order share, shrinking the baseline coverage gap and distorting subsidy-risk shortfalls.
Later service tasks selected the Task 6 top-eight report instead of the full subsidy-risk pool, and service sensitivity was further distorted by label-splitting and signed-gap sorting errors.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent did not implement the explicitly required relevant-unit construction and decision rule. It created top_commission15 as a bare limit on unit_rates rather than the 15 eligible units sorted by commission_first, and its diagnose condition allowed any clear-quality unit without requiring commercial meaningfulness, changing the decision state and examples.
error_labels.evidence: The reference has counts advance 3, diagnose 15, hold 12 with Chipotle in advance and Parm and RedFarm Broadway in diagnose, while the agent has diagnose 13 and hold 15, misses Chipotle and Parm, and includes Tamarind Tribeca and RedFarm Hudson.

error_labels.error_summary: The sensitivity calculation was applied to the already-wrong Task 3 decision pool, commercial rule, pressure counts, and decision_first labels. Under that inherited state the temporary missing-rating scoring was locally consistent, but it measured movement against the wrong baseline decisions.
error_labels.evidence: The reference has 10 moved units, while the agent reports 14 and includes lower-commission hold-to-diagnose moves such as Vanessa's Dumpling House, Junoon, and Tony's Di Napoli that arise from the wrong Task 3 decision state.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent computed the all-order high-value-customer share at the wrong unit of analysis, summing high-value customer rows and dividing by total orders instead of measuring the share of ledger orders placed by high-value customers. The wrong Task 3 advance set also meant the task was checking an incorrect set of forward units.
error_labels.evidence: The reference all-order high-value order share is 30.5585% and flags Chipotle and Five Guys as weak reach, while the agent reports 7.8504% and an empty weak_reach_advance_units list.

error_labels.error_summary: The subsidy-risk report inherited the wrong Task 3 diagnose state and the wrong Task 5 weak-reach and coverage baseline. With the coverage gap baseline shrunk to about 0.0785 instead of about 0.3056, the ranking and main shortfall choices were distorted even though the current pooling and scoring procedure was locally reasonable under those inputs.
error_labels.evidence: The reference top risks include Parm and label every shown main_shortfall as customer_gap, while the agent omits Parm, adds Blue Ribbon Sushi Izakaya, and reports rating_shortfall for Sushi of Gari 46 and Han Dynasty.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent selected the Task 6 top-eight report as the subsidy-risk pool instead of the full subsidy-risk pool, then introduced a key-parsing bug by splitting labels with the regex pattern " | ", which produced keys such as restaurant_name_key equal to blue and caused empty joins. It therefore failed to evaluate the actual pool, and the selected report was already wrong from Task 6.
error_labels.evidence: The reference finds three flipped units, The Meatball Shop, P.J. Clarke's, and Cafe Habana, while the agent reports changed_service_units as an empty list after risk_keys7 produced malformed keys and risk_day_rates7 had zero rows.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent again used the Task 6 top-eight report rather than the full subsidy-risk service review, so several required units were never considered. When no unit crossed the risk boundary, it also treated service sensitivity as a signed day-minus-one-hour gap sorted descending instead of the largest absolute service-rate gap requested by the fallback comparison.
error_labels.evidence: The reference diagnostics start with P.J. Clarke's, Cafe Habana, The Meatball Shop, Sushi of Gari 46, Chipotle, Shake Shack, TAO, and RedFarm Broadway, while the agent lists Sushi of Gari Tribeca, Han Dynasty, Nobu Next Door, Blue Ribbon Sushi, and Blue Ribbon Sushi Izakaya among others.

main_failure_patterns: Task 3 used the Task 1 first-watch artifact as the source of pressure flags and commercial-threshold state for all relevant units, so non-watch top-commission units lost their commercial meaning and no units advanced.
Downstream tasks repeatedly reused the wrong Task 3 operating groups and the wrong Task 6 subsidy-risk pool, causing later candidate sets, movement counts, and service screens to drift.

Several later turns added new rule errors on top of the cascade, especially omitting candidate-pool filters, using the wrong customer-value cutoff population, and ignoring the Task 8 fallback to slow-rate-gap diagnostics.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent built the relevant decision pool but reused the first-watch table as the source of pressure flags and eligible commission threshold instead of the full Task 1 unit-pressure state. Non-watch high-commission units such as Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken, Chipotle, and Five Guys were treated as lower-commission diagnoses rather than balanced advances, and the decision counts and leading examples were therefore wrong.
error_labels.evidence: The reference has decision counts advance 3, diagnose 15, hold 12 with three balanced advance units, while the agent reported advance 0, diagnose 15, hold 15 and labeled top-commission units as lower_commission.

error_labels.error_summary: The answer inherited the wrong Task 3 decision labels and also reimplemented the sensitivity decision rule incorrectly by allowing any unit with clear negative-feedback quality to become diagnose even when it was not commercially meaningful. That violated the instruction to reuse the Task 3 advance/diagnose/hold rules and introduced extra hold-to-diagnose movers while missing true advance-to-diagnose movers from the corrected Task 3 state.
error_labels.evidence: The reference moved count is 10 and starts with Sushi of Gari Tribeca and Han Dynasty, while the agent reported 18 movers and included non-reference movers such as Vanessa's Dumpling House, Junoon, and Tony's Di Napoli.

error_labels.error_summary: The immediate reason for the empty answer was the inherited Task 3 operating state with no advance units, so the Task 5 reach calculation had no forward units to review. The turn also used the median spend among customers with at least six orders rather than the all-customer median total spend, which was a separate cutoff-population error in the current task.
error_labels.evidence: The reference weak-reach advance units are Chipotle Mexican Grill $1.99 Delivery and Five Guys Burgers and Fries, but the agent returned an empty weak_reach_advance_units list because its Task 3 advance set was empty.

error_labels.error_summary: The subsidy-risk pool used the wrong inherited candidate states: it projected keys from all Task 3 operating decisions instead of only diagnosis units, and it inherited the empty weak-reach result from Task 5. It also failed the current instruction for missing coverage results because it did not carry the all-order high-value share into the coverage gap calculation, so main_shortfall was based on feedback or service gaps instead of the required customer gap.
error_labels.evidence: The reference top subsidy risks are Blue Ribbon Sushi, Sushi of Gari 46, Shake Shack, Sushi of Gari Tribeca, Han Dynasty, The Meatball Shop, Parm, and Nobu Next Door, all with main_shortfall customer_gap, while the agent included Boqueria, 5 Napkin Burger, Vanessa's Dumplings, and Sarabeth's East and reported missing_feedback or service_drag shortfalls.

error_labels.error_summary: The day-type service comparison was locally aimed at the subsidy-risk units, but it was run over the already-wrong Task 6 subsidy-risk pool. That wrong pool introduced extra units whose service flags flipped under the relative screen.
error_labels.evidence: The reference flipped units are The Meatball Shop, P.J. Clarke's, and Cafe Habana, while the agent included those three plus Junoon, L'Express, and Mamoun's Falafel from the incorrect subsidy-risk pool.

error_labels.error_summary: The turn inherited wrong coverage and service-pool artifacts from Tasks 6 and 7, which made some service-flag changes look like boundary crossings. Independently, it failed the explicit Task 8 fallback: when no unit crosses the boundary, the report should list slow-rate-gap diagnostics, but the agent filtered only units whose service flag changed and reported boundary crossings.
error_labels.evidence: The reference service_only_change_count is 0 and lists eight risk-state diagnostics led by P.J. Clarke's and Cafe Habana, while the agent reported boundary_crossing_count 3 and only six service-flag-sensitive units, including non-reference units Junoon, L'Express, and Mamoun's Falafel.

main_failure_patterns: The only incorrect turn was a final-answer reporting omission: the agent computed the correct ranked country-sector rows but omitted a required support field from the response.
The failure was not a long-horizon state or cascade issue because it occurred in the first task and the executed table already contained the missing field.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent identified the correct top five country-sector pairs and computed the pressure components correctly, but its final answer omitted loan_count for each pair. The task asked for the component values explaining why the pairs rose to the top, and the reference answer includes loan_count as the raw support behind the loan-scale component, so the response was incomplete even though the underlying executed report contained the field.
error_labels.evidence: The reference top_pressure_pairs include loan_count values 4630, 5183, 5670, 5977, and 2614, while the agent final answer lists the same pairs and matching scores but no loan_count field.

main_failure_patterns: The agent computed the correct top-five country-sector rows and early_pressure scores but reported transformed scoring components instead of the raw evidence fields required by the reference answer.
The only incorrect task was the first task, so the error was local to the current answer rather than a long-horizon state, memory, or cascade failure.

error_labels.error_summary: The agent correctly built the early pressure ranking and identified the same five country-sector pairs, but it did not report the requested component evidence on the expected raw scales. Instead of reporting completion_pct, avg_wait_days, and avg_term_months for funding completion, waiting time, and repayment term, it reported completion_gap, wait_burden, and term_burden. This is a current-task output failure with a metric-scale misunderstanding, not a coding, state-management, context-memory, or cascade error.
error_labels.evidence: The reference answer lists completion_pct, avg_wait_days, avg_term_months, borrower_reliance, and named_region_pct for each top pair, while the agent answer lists completion_gap, wait_burden, term_burden, borrower_reliance, and named_region_share despite matching the pairs and early_pressure values.

cost_comparisons.cost_goal: No general guarantee. History is cheaper on Luna and more expensive on Terra; the equal-or-lower-cost goal is not satisfied in both pairs.

main_failure_patterns: The agent often identified the right high-level workflow but changed a gating condition or fallback rule inside the dataflow, producing plausible outputs with wrong membership.

The largest long-horizon failure was incorrect reuse of prior customer-coverage state: Task 6 recomputed coverage for all units instead of preserving the Task 5 verified coverage artifact and the unproven-coverage rule.
A later rollback/sensitivity task inherited the wrong Task 6 coverage state while also introducing a fresh current-turn reporting error for service-screen diagnostics.

The agent repeatedly used the wrong inherited customer-coverage artifact, recomputing reach for all units instead of preserving the limited Task 5 first-customer coverage state and treating missing coverage as unproven.
The agent misapplied service-screen semantics by comparing day-type-relative slow rates against an incorrect local baseline and then letting those wrong service flags drive later boundary decisions.
Several wrong answers came from violating explicit current-turn formulas or gates while otherwise using the intended broad workflow.

manual_findings.mechanism: Luna control Task 3 changes the baseline population and operating gate
manual_findings.evidence: t03 step 6 wires unit_rates (all units) instead of eligible_units into the eligible threshold input. The top-commission limit lacks its required sort, and diagnose allows quality-clear units outside the commercial gate.
manual_findings.judging: Real computation/state-selection errors; Task 1 and Task 2 pass.

manual_findings.mechanism: Luna history Task 3 uses filtered watch-list evidence for a broader population
manual_findings.evidence: relevant_with_watch reads first_watch rather than pressured_units. The eligible commercial threshold is attached only to matching watch-list units, leaving non-watch candidates without it. The answer has 0 advance units instead of 3.
manual_findings.opportunity: Inspect the producer, incoming edges and population before reusing a filtered report as a lookup.

manual_findings.mechanism: Luna control Task 5 mixes customer counts and order counts
manual_findings.evidence: all_value_totals5 sums a customer-level 0/1 flag and divides by summed customer order counts. Offline raw-data check: 149 high-value customers; 580 high-value orders; 1898 orders. 149/1898 = 7.8504%, while 580/1898 = 30.5585%.
manual_findings.judging: An independently verified grain error; history cannot correct that formula.

manual_findings.mechanism: Luna history Task 6 loses an independent global baseline
manual_findings.evidence: subsidy_with_coverage6 reads weak_reach_scored, which is empty after the Task 3 error. score_subsidy6 fills both absent unit coverage and absent all_high_value_share with zero. Missing unit coverage should be zero, but the global baseline must come from all_customer_value_share.
manual_findings.opportunity: Retrieve the scalar producer separately; do not infer a global baseline from a filtered coverage table.

manual_findings.mechanism: Luna control Task 7 selects a limited report and splits labels as a regex
manual_findings.evidence: The source is the Task 6 top-eight report, then str.split(" | ", n=1) treats the delimiter as regex alternation and creates malformed keys. Result joins have zero rows.
manual_findings.opportunity: Preserve explicit key columns and use the full pool requested by the user.

manual_findings.mechanism: Terra first-task failure includes a judge inconsistency
manual_findings.evidence: Both rank the same five Kiva pairs with all five early-pressure scores correct. Control reports matching completion, wait, term, borrower and named-region values. Its judge requires loan_count. The history judge explicitly calls loan_count optional, while penalizing different raw-field omissions.
manual_findings.judging: Preserve binary scores. Separate correct ranking/calculation from final-output completeness; the control loan_count requirement is disputed.

manual_findings.mechanism: Codex cutoff note is real but inactive on this dataset
manual_findings.evidence: History Task 5 uses the 6-plus-customer spend median. The order-count 90th percentile is 3, so every customer with at least 6 orders already meets the frequency rule. This difference cannot change the high-value set here.
manual_findings.judging: The actual Task 5 history failure is the empty advance state inherited from Task 3, not this redundant branch.

manual_findings.mechanism: Prior answers are available but replayed redundantly
manual_findings.evidence: Every prior answer occurs three times in each final-task model context: assistant text, Answer tool argument, and tool observation. None is missing.
manual_findings.source: final task inputMessages in every arm
manual_findings.opportunity: Remove synthesized Answer echoes while retaining the original tool action, outcome and complete append-only history.
